transcripts.transcript:
Hello, Adrian Lim. This is Rachel Koh. We have our arranged telephone discussion. Is this still a convenient time to speak? I have your account summary available, and we can keep the conversation focused.

Yes, timing quite good. The warehouse team handling things downstairs, so I can sit quietly with my papers. My identification number is T three one two three one zero two L. My date of birth is 31 January 1994.

Thank you. It helps to have a quiet window between business commitments. How are your plans to spend more time on community activities coming along?

Still trying to make space lah. I help with the neighbourhood food collection, but sometimes the office calls and I have to disappear halfway. My family says I should let the staff handle more. They can manage; it's me who keeps checking the phone.

It sounds as though finding uninterrupted time is the practical challenge. We can arrange banking conversations around your business diary rather than contact you while you are supervising deliveries.

That would help. During dispatch, even finding the right paper also difficult. Today I brought the account summary into my office already. My overall account value on this summary is 1,000,000 Singapore dollars. That's just the account total, not the amount for this sale. The holding I want to reduce is Harbor SGD Bond Fund. I want to sell from my existing holding, not exit the whole position.

Your objective is to free up cash for your upcoming personal commitments while reducing your exposure to bond-market fluctuations. With Harbor SGD Bond Fund, rising market interest rates can lower the market value of the bonds it holds, which can reduce the fund's net asset value. Do you understand how rising interest rates could reduce the value of your holding in this fund?

Yes, I understand. Interest rates go up, the bonds it holds can drop in value, so my holding can be worth less.

The transaction charge for this sale is 0.2%. You could lose some or all of the capital you invested in this fund. Selling below your purchase value would crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept investment losses, including a loss crystallised by selling this holding?

Yes, I'm willing to accept that loss. Having the cash available for my commitments is more important to me.

For illustration only, a hypothetical sale of 10,000 Singapore dollars would release cash and reduce the remaining holding. That is an example, not your transaction amount. I recommend reducing your holding in Harbor SGD Bond Fund because it releases cash for your commitments and reduces your remaining exposure to interest-rate and credit-market fluctuations.

Let me get the handwritten page, not the account summary. My desk looks tidy until I actually need something, then cannot find. Here it is. For the settlement currency, use the— Use Singapore dollars for this transaction. The amount I want for this sale is 500,000. For the quantity, make it 1,500 units. Place it as a market order, please.

Can you explicitly confirm that the final transaction instruction you have just given me is what you want us to carry out?

Hmm, let me look through my notes a bit first ah.

Take your time. I will stay on the line while you review your notes. There is no need to rush your reply.

The writing in the margin a bit cramped. I was at the warehouse when I wrote it, with people coming in and out. Better I look properly than try to talk while hunting through the pages.

Of course. I can remain quiet while you check. If you need to return to work, we can arrange another conversation around your availability instead.

No need to arrange anything yet. Office door closed, so at least nobody interrupting now. Just give me a moment with this page.

Certainly. I'm here when you are ready.
